links.outcome: Stability of LLM diagnostic correction across demographic and contextual token variants
links.effect: Across 2,200 generated variants, stability across demographic and contextual variants was inconsistent, with some models showing spurious performance shifts based on non-clinical tokens.
links.quote: Stability across demographic and contextual variants was inconsistent, with some models showing spurious performance shifts based on non-clinical tokens.

links.outcome: LLM ability to correct erroneous physician diagnosis across high-stakes conditions
links.effect: Correction rates ranged from 20.0% (DeepSeek V3) to 55.0% (Gemini 2.5 Pro); most models failed to correct errors in syphilis, spinal epidural abscess, and myocardial infarction.
links.quote: Performance was strikingly consistent at the disease level; most models failed to correct errors in syphilis, spinal epidural abscess, and myocardial infarction.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM diagnostic correction to non-clinical input variations
links.effect: Performance was sensitive to non-clinical context; some models showed spurious performance shifts across 2,200 demographic and contextual variants.
links.quote: Stability across demographic and contextual variants was inconsistent, with some models showing spurious performance shifts based on non-clinical tokens.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs as an adversarial diagnostic second-opinion safety net to challenge clinician diagnoses
Adversarial multi-agent workflows prioritizing skepticism over agreement to reduce LLM confirmation bias

screen.reason: The study benchmarks 16 LLMs on their ability to identify and correct human diagnostic errors across 200 clinical vignettes and perturbed variants, evaluating intrinsic model performance and bias without testing an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
